expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Not really — that modal won't actually protect anyone."

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "confirmation dialogs that users see repeatedly become invisible. People develop click-through blindness and hit 'Confirm' reflexively."

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "1. Make it reversible (best) — Soft-delete workspaces... Add a 'Trash' where deleted workspaces live for 30 days"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "2. Grace-period undo — Delete immediately, show 'Workspace deleted. Undo' toast for 10 seconds... No friction on happy path"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "3. Require proportional action — Type the workspace name to confirm: DELETE production-api... Only use for truly irreversible, high-blast-radius actions"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: "4. Specific consequence dialog — 'Delete workspace Q4-analytics and 127 dashboards permanently?'"

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No claim about server-side enforcement; backend is mentioned only as a capability question ('does your backend support soft-delete or versioning?'), not as the layer that must enforce the rules rather than the UI.

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "Here's the poka-yoke ladder for destructive actions, strongest first" with numbered 1–4 and '(best)'
